edges.note: Companion placement edge for subfield:process-philosophy, proposed in this batch's nodes file. Chosen as a direct child of field:philosophy rather than nested under subfield:metaphysics, matching how every other philosophical school currently in this corpus is placed -- see that node's own uncertainty field for the explicit reasoning against inventing a §13 dual-membership placement here.
edges.rationale: Process philosophy is, on every source I know of, a school within philosophy rather than a topic spanning multiple fields -- the same structural logic this corpus's reviewed edges already apply to existentialism, phenomenology, pragmatism, critical-theory, scholasticism, analytic-philosophy, and continental-philosophy, all placed directly part_of field:philosophy. This edge follows that established pattern rather than inventing a new one.
edges.uncertainty: I have not live-fetched a UDC or LCC classification-schedule entry for process philosophy specifically this session -- the sibling edges this one mirrors were sourced to source:udc-summary/source:lcc-outline, and QC's live check should confirm process philosophy is actually listed (or listable) the same way, rather than accepting the structural-parity argument alone. Confidence (0.85) is set below the sibling edges' typical 0.9-0.95 for exactly this reason.

edges.source_hint: This repo's own reviewed data/node-translations.json entry for person:alfred-north-whitehead (read directly this session, reviewed: true): 'He created the philosophical school known as process philosophy, arguing that reality consists of processes rather than material objects and that processes are best defined by their relations with other processes; his Process and Reality is regarded as that school's foundational text.' A Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy entry and an Encyclopaedia Britannica entry on process philosophy are my recollection of standard reference coverage but neither is fetched this session [UNFETCHED].
edges.note: Closes the gap explicitly named in the prior wave's own proposal notes (foundry/proposals/person-wave12-v1/physics.nodes.proposed.json, an unreviewed artifact read this session): 'No edge is proposed toward Whitehead's best-known independent contribution, process philosophy: subfield:process-philosophy does not exist in the corpus... Recorded as an honest gap.' Sole founding, not co-founding -- unlike several other founder edges in this corpus (e.g. Pasteur/Koch on microbiology, Jakobson/Trubetzkoy on phonology), I am not aware of any other person standardly credited as a founder of this specific, named school, so no record-not-resolve plural-founding pattern is invoked here.
edges.rationale: The corpus's own already-reviewed translation for person:alfred-north-whitehead states directly, in origination language: 'He created the philosophical school known as process philosophy... his Process and Reality is regarded as that school's foundational text.' 'Created... the school' plus 'foundational text' is squarely founding language, not refinement or mere coining-a-term language, and Process and Reality (1929) is the referent's own point of origin rather than a predecessor tradition Whitehead merely named or extended -- so this claim does not run into the predates-the-founder exclusion this corpus has applied elsewhere (e.g. Whewell/uniformitarianism, held in foundry/held.json). Of my three assigned candidates this session, this is the strongest-sourced.
edges.uncertainty: My source is the corpus's own reviewed translation text, read directly this session, but I have not independently re-verified its underlying claim against a live SEP or Britannica source this session [UNFETCHED] -- QC's live check is load-bearing here, not a formality, same as every other edge in this batch. There is a longer intellectual lineage of 'process' thinking before Whitehead (Heraclitus's flux doctrine, Bergson's duree, William James's radical empiricism, C. S. Peirce's synechism) that some historians group into a broader 'process tradition' -- I am treating the founded_or_formalized claim as applying to the specific, named, institutionally continuous 20th-century school this corpus's subfield node is scoped to describe, which is standardly and specifically credited to Whitehead rather than to those earlier figures; if QC's live check finds mainstream sources crediting the school itself to an earlier figure, or treating Whitehead as one co-founder among several rather than the sole originator, this confidence should come down and a record-not-resolve co-founder edge may be the right correction. I have not verified whether anyone is ever named a co-founder of process philosophy specifically (as opposed to a precursor) -- this is the one place a plural-founding pattern could apply that I am not confident I have ruled out.

notes: person:alfred-north-whitehead -> subfield:metaphysics: NO EDGE proposed (candidate 3, adjudicated and declined). Metaphysics is an ancient branch of philosophy (Aristotle's Metaphysics, and centuries of scholastic and modern treatment before Whitehead), and subfield:metaphysics currently carries zero founder edges in /data (grep-confirmed this session: its only edge is edge:metaphysics-part-of-philosophy) -- consistent with the fact that no single person plausibly 'founded' a branch predating any candidate founder by two millennia. Whitehead's real, well-sourced originating contribution is the narrower subfield:process-philosophy (proposed in this batch), which sits within the broader territory of metaphysics but is not metaphysics itself. Crediting Whitehead with founding the whole of metaphysics would repeat the predates-the-founder failure this corpus has already ruled against for William Whewell/uniformitarianism (foundry/held.json, person-wave12-v1) and for the zero-edge treatment of Charles Lyell. A weaker `influenced` edge to subfield:metaphysics was also considered and declined: it would be a diffuse field-grain influence claim of the same shape this corpus has repeatedly held (foundry/held.json: Georges Cuvier->archaeology, Karl Pearson->sociology, Vladimir Vernadsky->environmental-science, Roman Jakobson->semiotics), and the more precise, better-sourced claim already exists at the process-philosophy grain in this same batch -- adding a second, broader edge alongside it would blur the record rather than sharpen it. This is an exclusion I am confident in, not merely a cautious one.

Considered and declined: person:martin-heidegger (candidate 4 -- a reviewed note naming an in-domain gap, found while reading this batch's context). edge:phenomenology-influenced-philosophy-of-technology (status: reviewed, data/edges.json, read this session) carries this verbatim note: 'Phenomenology (esp. Heidegger's "The Question Concerning Technology") is a founding tradition of philosophy of technology (postphenomenology, Ihde). Source = the tradition (Heidegger has no node). Direction correct.' That does name an honest gap by name. I am not proposing a Heidegger node in this batch, for a scope reason rather than a doubt about his notability or importance. This corpus's own standing rule holds that a person node needs the edge that earns its place, and Heidegger's two most obvious candidate targets both fail on inspection without further work: subfield:phenomenology is already founded_or_formalized by person:edmund-husserl (reviewed), and subfield:existentialism currently has no founder edge at all (only person:friedrich-nietzsche -influenced-> existentialism, reviewed) -- its own more standard founder candidates (Kierkegaard, Sartre) are themselves absent as corpus nodes. Proposing Heidegger into either slot without first working out that larger, currently open founder-of-existentialism question would be exactly the kind of under-researched bolt-on this contract asks generators to avoid. Recorded here as a real, separate gap worth its own dedicated wave -- existentialism's founder question (Kierkegaard / Sartre / Heidegger, none yet corpus nodes) and Heidegger's own node -- not silently dropped.
